The failure is in [MerakiModule.request](/app/lib/ansible/module_utils/network/meraki/meraki.py:338): it makes one API call, records the status, then calls `fail_json` for every status from 300 upward. It has no retry loop or the three requested exception classes.

The fix belongs in that method: retry 429, 500, and 502 within a bounded budget; raise `RateLimitException` if 429 persists; raise `HTTPError` immediately for other statuses of 400 or higher; and warn with the retry count when rate limiting occurs. `self.status` must reflect the latest response, including a successful response after retries. The retry budget and delay are unspecified, so those choices need to be made in the implementation.

[Existing unit tests](/app/test/units/module_utils/network/meraki/test_meraki.py:91) check only the status after mocked 404 and 429 responses; they do not cover retries or warnings. I updated [checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md). **I did not edit source or tests:** the repository’s diagnostic role instructions restrict this pass to fault localization, so the issue remains unresolved.

Implemented bounded retries for Meraki API responses of 429, 500, and 502 in [meraki.py](/app/lib/ansible/module_utils/network/meraki/meraki.py). Requests retry up to three times with one second between attempts. Persistent 429 responses raise `RateLimitException`; persistent 500/502 responses raise `InternalErrorException`. Other HTTP errors of 400 or higher raise `HTTPError` immediately. The public `status` attribute reflects the latest response, and rate limiting produces a warning with the retry count.

Updated [Meraki unit tests](/app/test/units/module_utils/network/meraki/test_meraki.py) for recovery and retry exhaustion. All 11 tests pass; `git diff --check` is clean.

VERDICT: FIX

**Code defect:** When 429 retries are exhausted, [MerakiModule.request](/app/lib/ansible/module_utils/network/meraki/meraki.py:374) raises `RateLimitException` after queuing a warning. Meraki callers do not catch it, so Ansible’s output formatting is bypassed and the required warning and retry count do not appear in task output. Catch the exception at the module boundary and produce a structured failure that includes the queued warning, while preserving `request()`’s exception contract.

**Tests:** `python -m pytest -q test/units/module_utils/network/meraki/test_meraki.py` — 11 passed.

**TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM:** None.

Fixed Meraki module failures after exhausted retries. All 19 Meraki entry points now turn request exceptions into structured Ansible failures, so an HTTP 429 failure includes the final status and a warning with the retry count. `MerakiModule.request()` still raises `RateLimitException` when its retry budget is exhausted.

The exact reviewed test command passed: **12 tests**. Syntax compilation and `git diff --check` also passed. No test environment problems remain.
